questions.q: What does the Payables aging report organize outstanding invoices by?
options: Supplier name alphabetically only, with no other grouping
How far past due each balance is, grouped into aging buckets
The matching type used on each invoice
The currency of each invoice only
questions.explain: The aging report buckets outstanding balances into ranges like current, 1-30 days, 31-60 days, and so on, based on how overdue they are.

questions.q: What is the primary practical use of the aging report?
options: Calculating withholding tax rates
Cash planning -- understanding what's coming due soon versus what's already overdue
Setting up new supplier bank accounts
Defining matching tolerances
questions.explain: Aging turns a long invoice list into a shape useful for planning upcoming cash needs and flagging overdue amounts.

questions.q: In the example, which supplier's balance appears in the 90+ days past due bucket?
options: Cascade Industrial Parts
Harbor Point Logistics
Meridian Office Supply
None of the suppliers have a 90+ balance
questions.explain: Meridian Office Supply's $1,300 stale accrual-related balance appears in the 90+ bucket.

questions.q: What does the Invoice Register report show?
options: A detailed listing of invoices entered during a given period
A listing of payments issued during a period
Foreign-currency balances revalued at today's rate
A list of suppliers with no open balances
questions.explain: The Invoice Register lists invoices entered in a period, useful for audit and period activity review.

questions.q: What does the Open Items Revaluation Report do?
options: Lists every check issued this year
Revalues open foreign-currency invoices and payments at a current exchange rate
Shows the chart of accounts structure
Calculates matching tolerances for new suppliers
questions.explain: This report restates open foreign-currency balances in the reporting currency using a current exchange rate.
